notes: 60 GHz pulsed-coherent radar (single Tx / single Rx A111 antenna-in-package) on a 33 mm round IoT module with nRF52840 MCU and Bluetooth 5; 1-D distance/presence sweeps with no measured angle. Default max measurable distance 7.0 m (MUR 6), 12.7 m with MUR 9. Sibling XM123 (18.6 x 15 mm, 1.71–1.89 V, UART/I2C) supports only the Sparse presence service. Optional CA122 casing is IP66. SDK login-gated under licence.

Solder-down LGA module (STM32L431 MCU + Acconeer A121 60 GHz pulsed-coherent radar, single Tx/Rx antenna-in-package) giving 1-D distance, presence and speed along boresight; no azimuth or elevation. FoV values are antenna half-power beamwidths. Range resolution 43 mm is the A121 Profile 1 figure at 25 °C (up to 346 mm in Profile 5); frame rate typically 1-100 Hz, power milliwatt-class. The bare A121 sensor was US$16.74 at the same distributor.

76-77 GHz long-range 4D imaging radar (6Tx x 8Rx cascade, built for Ainstein by Beijing Muniu Technology) for FCW/ACC/AEB; up to 2048 point-cloud detections plus 50-60 tracked objects per frame. Azimuth resolution 3.6° normal / 1.8° super-resolution; velocity accuracy ±0.027 m/s; elevation accuracy ±0.1° at boresight. 8-pin TE automotive connector; no public message ICD. 77 GHz long-range 4D imaging radar sold by Ainstein as I-79; the FCC-filed user manual for 2ATMB-I7948 is a Beijing Muniu Technology product brochure (model I-79-48). Outputs up to 2048 point-cloud detections and 50-60 tracked objects per 60 ms cycle; azimuth resolution 3.6° (1.8° super-resolution). Distributor sensing.ai lists it at $4,000.

Previous-generation 77 GHz long-range ADAS radar (FCC grant band only 76.3–76.482 GHz). Outputs up to 40 Kalman-filtered tracked objects; CAN message definitions published in the user manual, DBC on request. Power <4 W; 12 V supply only. Mount 30–80 cm above road; automatic alignment needs on-road driving above 25 km/h.

interface: 2x CAN (private object bus + vehicle bus), ISO 11898, UDS
notes: 77 GHz mid/long-range front radar (3Tx/4Rx), rebadged Muniu K77-G3; K-77-G3-12 (12 V) and K-77-G3-24 (24 V) share one FCC grant. Outputs up to 40 Kalman-filtered objects (X/Y, motion class) per frame on a private CAN bus; DBC available on request. Auto-alignment requires on-road driving above 25 km/h. Supply range shown is for the 12 V variant.

77 GHz 4D imaging radar (FCC grant 2ATMB-O79V3, 76.1-80.9 GHz). Base version outputs over CAN 2.0 (250 kbit/s default); Pro adds 10/100 Ethernet (UDP/TCP) with raw and filtered spherical point clouds (range, speed, azimuth, elevation) and tracked objects; max output targets Base 10 / Pro 15. Values from the 2024 data sheet; the older brochure lists 77-81 GHz, <0.2 m range resolution, 5.7° azimuth resolution, 10 Hz, 12 V, <10 W, -40..+85 °C and 95 x 160 x 48.2 mm, and the FCC manual states an 8-26 VDC supply up to 12 W. Elevation resolution 18° is from the older brochure. ISO 61508 SIL2 claimed. Distributor sensing.ai lists $3,500 (shown out of stock in a later product feed); an O-79 Eval Kit is listed at the same price.

First-generation 77 GHz blind-spot (rear-corner) radar, classical CAN at 500 kbit/s; up to four units per bus addressed as FL/FR/RL/RR. 2D only (±4° elevation fan, no elevation output). Power 3 W; 10-pin Molex connector; 50 ms frame. Open-source BSD-3 ROS driver from the maker includes the CAN map. Superseded by the CAN-FD T-79 Gen 3 (FCC ID 2ATMB-T79G3B).

Gen-3 79 GHz RFCMOS corner radar (3Tx/4Rx, built by Beijing Muniu) for BSD/LCA/RCTA/DOW; outputs up to 64 tracked targets over CAN-FD with UDS diagnostics; up to four units per bus. Ainstein's own 2024 T-79 datasheet (76-79 GHz, 0.3-110 m, 0.30 m resolution, 6° azimuth resolution, 9-16 V) describes a differently specified variant. Designed for mounting behind a plastic bumper (≤2 dB one-way loss).

77 GHz 16Tx x 16Rx 4D imaging radar (TI AWR2188 + TDA4VEN, waveguide antenna). Selectable range profiles named 150 m, 320 m and 620 m; spec-sheet figures are for the 320 m configuration. Latency <60 ms; gPTP/IEEE 1588 time sync. The setup guide asks for a >25 W supply although the spec sheet lists 18 W; spec sheet is titled preliminary.

interface: GMSL2 (radar head) to RCU; RCU outputs 100BASE-T1 Ethernet (UDP)
notes: 8Tx8Rx corner imaging radar head; requires the Altos RCU (head speaks GMSL2, RCU outputs 100BASE-T1 UDP) and runs in pairs or fours. Four range modes: 150/150/300/300 m with range resolution 0.05/0.1/0.07/0.14 m and up to 4000/2000/3000/1500 points per frame. Head 4 W, RCU 10 W (RCU 105 x 86 x 26 mm, 255 g, no IP rating); latency <40 ms; shock/vibration ISO 16750; elevation accuracy 0.4°. Public ROS1/ROS2 drivers carry no licence. Spec sheet labelled preliminary.

Four-chip cascaded (TI AWR2243 x4 + TDA4, 12Tx/16Rx) 4D imaging radar for forward-facing autonomous-driving use. Two range modes: 320 m (1.4 m range resolution) and 80 m (0.35 m). Speed accuracy 0.02 m/s, elevation accuracy 0.15°, data latency <40 ms, ISO 16750 shock/vibration, ASIL B; PTP time sync. Point output carries per-point elevation; RCS in linear m²; wire frame z-down. FCC grant band 77.45–77.98 GHz with 25 cm separation and no co-location; maker offers separate software for 2–4 radars on different frequencies. Minimum range not published by the maker. Four-chip cascaded (TI AWR2243 + TDA4) 4D imaging radar. Two range modes: 320 m (1.4 m range resolution, 0.2 m accuracy) and 80 m (0.35 m resolution, 0.05 m accuracy). Speed accuracy 0.02 m/s, elevation accuracy 0.15°, data latency <40 ms, ISO 16750 shock/vibration, ASIL B, PTP time sync and external trigger. Minimum range not published.

4D imaging radar reference/evaluation platform (B0 sample board) built on Arbe's chipset with 2,304 virtual channels; sold to Tier-1 radar makers and OEMs. 2026 Phoenix spec: 0.7° azimuth / 0.9° elevation resolution, 120° x 30° FoV, 300 m, 20+ FPS, over 100,000 detections per frame. The US grant covers 76-77 GHz only (measured 99% OBW ~317 MHz), narrower than the chipset's 76-81 GHz capability. Point cloud over Ethernet, tracks over CAN; ROS 2 Sensor Integration Toolbox offered by the vendor; ICD under NDA.

interface: CAN FD (1 channel, up to 5 Mbit/s)
notes: Manufacturer in administration (2024); catalogue offline. 77 GHz 3TX/4RX FMCW sensor with software-defined ultra-short, medium and long-range modes; ultra-short-range (factory default) mode detects 0.04-12 m, medium-range mode to 150 m (5 dBsm target), manual states 0.05-225 m overall. Conflicts between the FCC manual (CC-1010090-AA) and the later catalogue (CC-1010090-AD): temperature +75 vs +85 °C, velocity 0-92 km/h vs -75..+75 km/h, range resolution 0.039 m vs 0.026-0.8 m (mode dependent), velocity resolution 0.32 vs 0.16-0.4 m/s; typical power <5 W, max 12.5 W; FCC test report lists 12 V and 24 V nominal rails. Connector JAE MX44006SF1, 6-way.

77 GHz long-range 4D radar (stepped-FM pulse compression), 12 V nominal; functions deactivated above 18 V. Standard configuration 0.2-301 m; extended range mode up to 1514 m with limited resolution. Output: RDI detection list (range, azimuth, elevation, radial velocity, RCS; up to 800 per cycle) and object list (up to 200 objects). Operation above +65 °C requires additional cooling; open mounting without a radome is not supported. Public ROS 2 drivers: tier4/nebula (Apache-2.0) and robotics-upo/ars548_ros; vendor ROS 2 node is licence-dongle protected.

Gen-4 77 GHz long-range radar (FCC HVIN ARS4-C, marketing name ARS441); multi-scan field of view ±9° to 250 m, ±45° to 70 m, ±75° to 20 m; 60 ms cycle; elevation measurement capability. 12 V nominal (FCC test 6.5-19.0 V), 8 W. Series OEM part (certified unit ARS441DP); plastic housing with moulded radome, mounts behind a fascia. Operational description and array details are permanently confidential.

Gen-6 77 GHz long-range front radar (4Tx/4Rx single chip, launch-on-package waveguide antenna) configured as an RDI (ISO 23150) detection sensor for external fusion; 280 m for cars, 140 m for pedestrians; speed accuracy ±0.08 kph. 1.3° azimuth resolution applies only with the high-resolution technique enabled. Alibaba price is from a Hong Kong trading company (not an authorised distributor) for a unit labelled ARS620BY2S / Model ARS6-A without FCC marking. Sixth-generation 4T4R single-chip long-range radar, configured as an ISO 23150 radar detection interface (RDI) sensor; maker describes it internally as '3.5D'. Range 280 m for cars, 140 m for pedestrians; near-range FoV ±60° also cited in press. Speed accuracy ±0.08 km/h. Range resolution (0.2 m) and 1.3° azimuth resolution (high-resolution mode) come from Chinese press interviews with the maker, not a datasheet. Minimum range and IP rating not published; installation requires ≥20 cm separation from people.

77 GHz short-range corner radar (gen-5); FCC user manual describes a short-range scan up to 12.6 m and a far-range scan up to 99 m, both ±90°. Interface conflict: the AUMOVIO SRR52x product page lists an Ethernet interface while the AUMOVIO engineering-solutions page and the public Tier IV Nebula ROS 2 driver use CAN FD. Range resolution 0.2 m (near scan) / 1 m (far scan) is from a third-party distributor spec page. Marketplace offer (MOQ 5; $380 at 5-99, $350 at 100-499, $290 at 500+) has since been delisted. Fifth-generation 77 GHz corner radar; alternates a short-range scan (to 12.6 m, ±90°) and a far-range scan (to 99 m, ±90°); ±75° measurement FoV. Outputs 2D detections (range, azimuth, range rate, RCS, SNR, false-alarm flags) and objects over CAN FD; expects host velocity/yaw-rate input. Nominal supply 13.5 V. Engineering samples sold as SRR 520DI (quote-only). Open-source ROS 2 driver (tier4 nebula, Apache-2.0); official ICD under NDA.

Gen-6 77 GHz corner/short-range radar family (entry SRR620, premium SRR630), filed as SRR6-A (FCC OAYSRR6A, ISED 4135A-SRR6A, 76-77 GHz). FoV stated as ±90° detection / ±75° measurement (current page: ±81°); 200 m for cars, 110 m for pedestrians; speed accuracy ±0.07 kph. The related SRR6-B (FCC OAYSRR6B, marketed SRR630FD) adds a 77-81 GHz high-bandwidth mode (0.04-0.05 m range resolution, 10 Hz) and is a separate variant. Sixth-generation 77 GHz corner/surround radar (4Tx/4Rx waveguide antenna, gen-6 SRR600 family) certified as SRR6-A (76–77 GHz only); family page lists ±81° FoV, 200 m range, RDI/object list/free-space output over 100 Mbps Ethernet with MACsec and CAN-FD. Pedestrian range 110 m and 0.29 m range resolution are from Chinese press; ±30° elevation sensing from a press road test. 70 x 55 x 20 mm without connector. Grant requires 20 cm separation and forbids co-location. No public ICD; sold as SRR 630RDI engineering samples on quote.

77 GHz side/turn-assist radar (Autel ASR110 is an FCC change-in-identification of the ASR100; specs from the ASR100 datasheet). Two modes: slow speed (0.25 m minimum range, 0.31 m resolution, ±60 km/h) and high speed (0.9 m minimum, 0.96 m resolution, ±150 km/h); 80 m for vehicles, 40 m for pedestrians/cyclists. Outputs detections and warnings over CAN FD; static objects are not reported. Storage −40…+105 °C. Configuration via Windows tool; no public ICD.

Pole/wall-mounted 60 GHz surveillance radar for area and traffic monitoring; outputs classified, tracked moving objects (human/vehicle/unknown) via VAPIX/ONVIF metadata; static objects are not reported. Detection 5–60 m for humans, 5–90 m for vehicles; mounting height 3.5–12 m. PoE (802.3at) or 10–28 V DC; IK10, NEMA 4X; up to 8 radars per 350 m coexistence zone; indoor low-power and outdoor modes.

interface: IO-Link v1.1, discrete and analog outputs (M12 5-pin)
notes: Industrial 60 GHz FMCW distance/presence sensor (TI IWR6843AOP inside) reporting one distance to a selected target plus signal strength over IO-Link (48-bit process data), discrete or analog outputs; no angle or velocity output. Three SKUs; 10–30 V DC (KUQ variant 12–30 V). Linearity <±10 mm below 0.3 m, <±4 mm above; not for personnel protection. Configuration via Windows software and PRO-KIT.

60 GHz industrial radar distance/presence sensor (TI IWR6843AOP based). Over IO-Link it reports distance, beam angle (-60..+60°) and radial velocity for two configurable switch channels, plus discrete/analog outputs; no elevation. Max velocity ±9 m/s in Fast/Medium response (±4.5 m/s Slow). IP67 and IP69K; manufacturer states it must not be used for personnel protection. A separate 77 GHz Q90R2 variant exists under FCC ID UE3Q90R2-7. Industrial FMCW distance/presence radar in 60 GHz (Q90R2-12040-6K*Q, FCC ID UE3Q90R2-6) and 77 GHz (Q90R2-12040-7KDQ, FCC ID UE3Q90R2-7) versions with the same published performance. Reports up to two selected targets (distance, velocity, one angle, signal strength) with configurable detection windows; outputs via IO-Link, discrete and analog. Velocity range ±9 m/s in fast/medium response modes (±4.5 m/s slow); 12-30 V for analog-voltage models.

interface: IO-Link (120-bit process data), 2x discrete PNP/NPN, pulse-frequency output; M12 5-pin
notes: Industrial 77 GHz FMCW radar (TI IWR1843 inside) that reports, per output channel, the distance, beam angle and velocity of one taught target (nearest or strongest) over IO-Link, two discrete outputs or a pulse-frequency output. Three response modes (50/150/250 ms) with ±9/±9/±4.5 m/s maximum velocity. Configurable radial (±10°…±50°) or rectangular detection window. MIL-STD-202G vibration, IK08; not for personnel protection. FCC grant is Part 95 (vehicular use).

122-123 GHz off-highway radar distance sensor with a 6° pencil beam (about 9° at 20 dB): 1-D distance, confidence and radial speed only, no angle. Variants: DAH5 single-object (8.5 m) and multi-object (up to 8 objects, speed field -4 to +3.97 m/s), DAE0 ground/crop (5 m). Output period settable (0.2-100 Hz). Manufacturer states it must not be used in direct machine control. The related R670V (77-81 GHz, FCC PGP-R670V, 21 firmware variants) was granted 2026-08-18 but is not on sale.

77 GHz 4D imaging radar, 12TX/16RX (four radar ICs). Operating modes DR, LR, MR, SR (FCC Class II filing: SR 2.1 GHz, MR 1.95 GHz, LR 1.6 GHz sweep bandwidth). Outputs ISO 23150 RDI detections (range, azimuth, elevation, velocity) over SOME/IP; open BSD-3 SDK and ROS 2 driver (Humble/Jazzy); up to 4 sensors per SDK instance; PTP time sync. Velocity window is the default ambiguity domain in the driver message definition. A marketplace listing states 8-25 V and 76-79 GHz.

60 GHz sleep/presence sensor (Infineon BGT60TR13C class, 1Tx/3Rx) sold in Korea as Wellune MOD611 (later 'wellune A1'). Outputs four states only (absence, presence, motion, apnea) via Wi-Fi/Bluetooth to a cloud sleep API; tracks one person (the one with larger movement). Detection ranges by angle: movement 3.8/2.3/1.2 m; presence/apnea 2.3/1.6/0.6 m. Indoor consumer enclosure, USB-A powered.

Bosch generation-5 'Front radar plus' ACC/AEB front radar (CAN + FlexRay variant), fitted in Mercedes-Benz and Stellantis vehicles; outputs an on-board environment model/object list. Product-line sheet also gives vertical angle accuracy 0.2° / separability 6°. Designed to be mounted behind a fascia; +85 to +95 °C restricted operation.

76-77 GHz off-highway imaging radar outputting a 4D point cloud of up to 1,024 locations per cycle (16 attributes each, including elevation, radial velocity and a 'standing' flag). Range accuracy/separability 0.11-0.22 m / 0.41-0.83 m depending on configuration; ISO 13849 compliant; rear connector. Velocity range from the maker's public ROS 2 driver signal limits (Apache-2.0). Power: ~12 W typical (datasheet) vs max 11 W (product page); 12 V nominal. Off-highway radar from Bosch Engineering for construction/agricultural machines. Range separability 0.41–0.83 m (mode dependent; range accuracy is a separate, finer figure); up to 1024 locations per cycle with 16 attributes each; ROS 2 support stated; 12 V supply with a converter for other rails.

77 GHz CAN object-detection radar for commercial/off-highway vehicles; reports objects (polar radius/angle, X/Y, relative speed) in 2-D only. Detection area 60 m x 16 m; static objects reported only beyond about 1.5 m; two objects separate at ≥0.8 m range and >0.7 m/s velocity difference. Up to 8 sensors per bus; typ. 0.23 A at 12 V; shock 51 g, vibration 8.3 g. The maker warns it should not be solely relied upon to detect people. The FCC grant (product code BACKSENSE10) covers the BS-9100 and BS-8100 families; there is no model 'BS-10000'.

Forward long-range 77 GHz automotive radar, 4T4R, ASIL B, 40 tracked targets. Sold on Alibaba by Zilai Technology (ZLY); the Luda LDMR220 drone obstacle-avoidance radar publishes an identical spec table. Alibaba listing states a 76-77 GHz bandwidth while the maker page states 76-79 GHz. Sample price $168 retrieved 2026-09-24; minimum order 5 pieces at the same base price.

77 GHz dual-cascade 4D imaging front radar. Two documented revisions: current web table (8T8R listed on EN page, 350 m, 0.076 m range resolution, 12/24 V, 12 W, 130 g, 17.3 mm thick) and a Nov-2025 6T8R manual (0.2–360 m, 0.15 m resolution, 12 V, ≤10 W, 150 g, 19.3 mm, max 2048 points/frame and 256 tracks); the Chinese page lists 6T8R. Current page: 81920 points/s, speed accuracy ±0.022 m/s, elevation accuracy ±0.1°, ASIL B. The manual's connector pinout shows Ethernet only. Operating temperature not published; protocol supplied with purchase only. Price is a reseller (LUDA) Alibaba listing.

interface: SerDes over coax (raw CSI-2 data, power over coax)
notes: 8T8R 77 GHz 'satellite' imaging front radar head (Tianqiong family with corner radar CTMRR-610): streams raw CSI-2 data over a SerDes coax link with power over coax; point cloud/tracks (up to 6144 points/frame, 30 Hz) are produced by the maker's software on a domain controller. Speed accuracy ±0.05 m/s; ASIL B. SerDes family and public ICD not published.

77 GHz 4T4R FMCW corner radar for rear-bumper BSD/LCA/DOW/RCW/CTA; ASIL-B; up to 64 tracked targets; elevation coverage ±12° but no per-detection elevation output documented. Listing price is from the Accio mirror of Alibaba offer 1601787267786 (MOQ 2).

interface: Bluetooth LE 5.0 (to CHIGEE displays) + warning-lamp outputs
notes: 77 GHz (76-76.4 GHz) motorcycle rear radar, 2Tx/4Rx, providing BSD, LCA, AOA and RCW rider alerts via side warning lamps and Bluetooth LE pairing to CHIGEE displays; no external detection data output. Activation speed selectable 0/10/30/50 km/h. The FCC RF test report records a manufacturer-declared 0-40 °C working range.

Indoor wall-mounted 60 GHz smart-home activity/presence appliance (mount ~48–52 in high, one per room). It computes a sparse 3D point cloud (x, y, z, velocity, SNR) internally at 10 fps but only metadata leaves the device, via Wi-Fi to a cloud REST API. A Chirp-authored study cites detection up to 8 m. Indoor use only, 5–95% RH non-condensing; supplied 12 V/3 A adapter. Leased by subscription rather than sold.

77 GHz corner radar (3Tx 4Rx) from Nanjing Chuhang Technology (product specification v1.4, 2024). Manual states 77-79 GHz operation, ±0.1 m range accuracy, 0.2 m/s velocity resolution, <1° angle accuracy, CAN interface and both target-output and point-cloud working modes; tracks up to 32 objects with position, velocity, height, class and RCS.

77 GHz two-wheeler (motorcycle) early-warning corner radar, 2Tx 3Rx with built-in IMU for body-posture compensation; outputs tracked targets classified as truck, car, two-wheeler or pedestrian. Angle accuracy ±0.1° at boresight, ±0.5° overall. Integrated cable design; product specification v1.2 (2024-12-11).

76-77 GHz 4D radar sold as a bare PCB (IP67 only when fitted in a housing, not supplied). Datasheet: 0.10-80 m (at 120°), 40 m at 15 dBsm in short-range performance; 200 tracked targets / 400 point-cloud points; operating current 200 mA (peak 370 mA) at 12 V. Speed row is labelled km/h but values are given in m/s. No interface/protocol document is published. The maker's sibling CRT-RV500-001 sheet matches the Nanoradar SR75 numerically.

1-inch evaluation cube built on TI AWR1843AOP (3Tx/4Rx antenna-on-package, 77–81 GHz, 4 GHz bandwidth) with CAN-FD; runs TI SDK demo firmware outputting x/y/z/velocity point clouds. Purchase grants an evaluation/development licence; production via the maker's ODM service. One sensor per CAN-FD bus (fixed message IDs); no IP rating. FCC limited single-modular grant tested in this host; the USB variant RS-1843AOPU has no grant of its own. Firmware, ICD and ROS 2 packages are login-gated.

1-inch cube 60 GHz antenna-on-package radar (TI IWR6843AOP, 3TX/4RX, 4 GHz bandwidth) with CAN-FD; sold by D3 for evaluation and proof-of-concept. FCC 2ASVZ-02 is a limited modular approval tied to host RS-6843AOPC. Sibling RS-6843AOPU (USB, 5 V, SKU 1002143) is also US$399; quick start guide lists 7-24 VDC at up to 1.0 A versus 6-24 VDC in the datasheet. No IP or temperature rating published.

Perimeter-security 'visual radar': 4 MP camera with an integrated 60 GHz radar (Cheng-Tech CTSGR-400 antenna module, 3Tx/4Rx) that tracks up to 64 moving humans/vehicles (distance, angle, speed, type) to 60 m within 120° horizontal; stationary objects outside the 0.72-80 km/h window do not trigger. Ethernet (Dahua SDK/API, ONVIF S) and RS-485; 12 V DC ±30% or PoE 802.3at. Requires hard ground and clear siting.

Indoor 60 GHz people-counting / dwell sensor for retail analytics; outputs tracked-person positions (X/Y/Z, proximity, paths) via a proprietary SDK or cloud REST API, no point cloud or velocity. Radar hardware is Shenzhen RadarEye ACMR6001 (4T3R). Forward range 0.3-5 m; side coverage up to 3 m each side (spec sheet Aug 2026) vs 2.5 m in the FCC manual. USB-C bus powered; mounting height 1.2-2 m.

interface: 3 solid-state relay outputs + test input; Bluetooth 5.1 for configuration
notes: 60 GHz radar presence/activation scanner for vehicle barriers ('virtual loop'): three floating MOSFET relay outputs (safety, opening, drive-through) plus test input, configured only via a Bluetooth app; no data interface. Range 8 m (6 m for EN 12453 protection level D person detection), detection angle ±60°, max object speed 30 km/h, reaction time 200 ms. Mount 0.3-0.9 m above road; avoid high-vibration locations.

Rear-facing motorcycle approach/blind-spot warning radar (TI AWR1843AOP based) sold as a kit with two indicator lights; it outputs only colour-coded alerts to Garmin's phone app or zumo navigator over Bluetooth, tracks up to 8 moving vehicles, and operates only while the motorcycle travels at 25-150 km/h. Velocity values are closing speed relative to the host. FCC grant lists three single-frequency radar channels (78.110 / 78.957 / 79.805 GHz).

Mining collision-avoidance 4D radar module: a re-housed smartmicro DRVEGRD 152 (6Tx/8Rx) in a 1 kg housing, powered and controlled through Hexagon's Smart Switch (1–6 modules per vehicle); installation by authorised installers only. Long-range mode 0.9–180 m and medium-range mode 0.33–66 m; speed accuracy ≤0.07 m/s. Vibration MIL-STD-810H 7.7 grms, shock 60 g. Grant forbids co-location except under multi-transmitter procedures.

Wall-mounted 4T3R human-tracking module (mount 2.2 m, tilted 10°). Host polls target list (ID, range, pitch, azimuth, X/Y) over UART; no velocity field. Protocol allows up to 10 target records per response while the spec states up to 8 persons. Storage −40…+85 °C. OEM board is Shenzhen RadarEye ACMR6001; A/B/C (4T4R) variants are different products.

Ceiling-mounted (2.5-3.0 m, antenna down) 60 GHz 4T4R human-trajectory module; tracks up to 10 people. Detailed UART protocol mode outputs per-person ID, X/Y/Z and Vx/Vy/Vz; point-cloud length is fixed at zero. Peak power 1.7 W; manufacturer's own store page showed US$28.60 (2026-09-18) versus US$27.34 on the Alibaba store.

60 GHz 4T4R ceiling-mount people-tracking module: tracks up to 10 people and reports X/Y/Z per person over UART; also detects stationary people. Range 0.5-8 m is defined at 2.7 m ceiling height (ground circle radius 3.5 m). Output coordinates are 1-byte values at 0.1 m granularity. Scan interval configurable 100-10000 ms. Price is for the bare module SKU (test kit SKU $29.99).

60 GHz respiration/heart-rate module (ADT6101P, 2T2R); documented mode measures a chest at 0.4–1.5 m. Target records carry x/y/z but Z is always 0; speed only as an unscaled dop_idx. Manufacturer spec states 58–62 GHz operating band vs FCC grant 57.998–60.594 GHz; FCC user-manual exhibit gives default baud 1382400 vs 115200 in spec V1.1. Board measured 25 x 23 x 0.8 mm in the vendor STEP model, conflicting with the 25 x 31.5 mm datasheet figure. Supply ripple ≤50 mV, ≥1 A source required.

60 GHz 2T2R presence module on the ADT6101P SoC; tracks up to 3 people with x/y/z output and also emits a 3D point cloud (message 0x0A08, per-point x/y/z and speed) over UART (115200 baud). Ceiling or side mount; ceiling detection area 5 m x 3 m at 2.7 m height, side-mount range 0-6 m. Supply current up to 600 mA. Price is for the bare module SKU ($16.75 for the kit SKU).

60 GHz 2T2R antenna-in-package human presence and tracking module (ADT6101P chip), tracks up to 3 people; side or ceiling mount. UART TinyFrame protocol outputs target messages (0x0A04) and point cloud (0x0A08) with x/y/z, Doppler index and cluster ID; velocity is given only as a Doppler index. Supply current 135 mA typical, 600 mA max.

60 GHz multi-lane traffic tracking radar (3Tx/4Rx, 12-element virtual array) reporting per-vehicle tracks with range, azimuth and speed (0–182 km/h either direction, including stopped vehicles); no elevation output. Built-in accelerometer and 5 MP aiming camera; 106 x 96 x 62 mm, 270 g; NEMA TS-2-2021 tested; M12 connector IP67. Binary protocol available under no-cost licence; C/C# SDK on request. Not a failsafe device.

60 GHz single-beam distance/velocity radar (InnoSenT IDR-2060 front end, lens antenna) outputting the selected target's distance, speed, power and RCS over IO-Link plus switching/analog outputs. Three modes: standard (0.1-20 m, 100 mm, ±6 m/s, 20 Hz), long range (0.25-35 m, 370 mm, ±15 m/s, 20 Hz) and fast (0.1-20 m, 100 mm, ±20 m/s, 100 Hz). FCC grant limits use to fixed operations; vehicular use prohibited. CAN J1939 variant R1D103 (-40...85 °C, 9-32 V) presumably under the same grant. UL Ta -40...65 °C.

77 GHz single-beam distance radar (40° x 20° aperture): outputs up to 128 point targets with radial distance, velocity, power and RCS but no angle. Modes: standard 0.1-20 m, 0.10 m resolution, ±6 m/s; long range / high velocity 0.25-50 m, 0.32 m resolution, ±15 m/s. Power max 9 W; UL rating limited to Ta -40...65 °C. IO-Link sibling R1D200 (10-30 V, up to 100 Hz) shares the FCC ID; ifm US store price US$805.80 for either variant (2026-09-21).

60 GHz area/distance radar with CAN SAE J1939 output; in distance mode it streams a point cloud with X/Y/Z, velocity, power and RCS for up to 128 reflections per frame. Interface (J1939 PGN map) is published in free ifm software manuals. IO-Link siblings R2D102 and R2D111 share FCC ID UN6-R2D1 but output only distance and velocity of a selected target; non-US sibling R2D101 adds a 0.25-30 m, ±15 m/s mode. Static objects closer than 1 m are not stably detected in area mode.

77-81 GHz area radar for mobile machines with two operating modes: standard (0.1-20 m, 100 mm range resolution, ±6 m/s) and long range/high velocity (0.25-35 m, 350 mm, ±15 m/s); 50 m range is referred to a reference reflector (E23014). Outputs up to 128 target reflections with X/Y/Z, velocity and static/dynamic information over CAN SAE J1939 (protocol documented in the public software manual). UL approval Ta -40...65 °C. Grant UN6-R2D2 covers the R2D2 family (76-81 GHz). 77 GHz area radar family under one FCC grant (UN6-R2D2): R2D201 (CAN J1939, point cloud with X/Y/Z, up to 128 reflections, static flag), R2D200 and R2D210 (IO-Link, single selected target). Standard mode 0.1-20 m / 100 mm / ±6 m/s; long-range mode 0.25-35 m / 350 mm / ±15 m/s; R2D210 covers 0.3-30 m. R2D203 / R2D205 are Japan / India radio variants. US price $999.60 per unit for each US SKU. DBC file referenced but not public.

Mechanically scanning 77 GHz mining radar: a motor-driven parabolic mirror sweeps a 4° pencil beam through a 360° plane at 3–50 rps (up to 12,000 measurements/s, 20 ms output delay); 2D profile only. Requires indurad RadarProcessingUnit; head cannot be used standalone. Detection range vehicles 120 m, bulk 60 m, persons 40 m. Sibling iSDR-H (same FCC grant family of 8 electronically identical devices): 1.5–1000 m, 24 V/20 W, 8.1 kg. Shock 50 g/11 ms; vibration 5–2000 Hz 10 g. Grant requires 40 cm separation.

60 GHz FMCW distance-measurement radar module with lens-fed 8° x 8° beam: outputs distance, velocity, direction and signal strength of targets in a UART target list (single-beam, no angle). Fill-level / anti-collision use; customer enclosure required. Public FCC user manual is a v0.9 preliminary; datasheet and interface protocol are login-gated. InnoSenT's web page advertises 62-64 GHz while the FCC grant covers 58.017-61.419 GHz.

60 GHz 1-D distance measurement system (single Tx/Rx patch behind a lens, 5.5° 3 dB beam): outputs a distance target list over UART, no angle and no velocity. Modes: single target 50 Hz, multi-target 10 Hz (10 targets) or 25 Hz (15 targets), long integration 4 Hz for static objects (max 20 m). Open module for integration in a customer housing (no IP rating). FCC grant limits use to collision-avoidance and level-measurement applications for fixed operations only. Power 1.3-1.6 W during constant acquisition.

interface: CAN (EN 50325-5) to control unit; control unit: OSSD, PROFIsafe/FSoE, MODBUS TCP
notes: Also certified under FCC ID 2ANOS-SBV01. 60 GHz SIL 2 / PL d safety radar sensor for machinery (Inxpect SRE 200 Series); works only with an Inxpect C2xx control unit (up to six sensors per unit). Coverage programmable 10-100° horizontal x 20° vertical, 0-5 m, up to four detection fields; outputs per field the nearest target's distance and azimuth (MODBUS TCP / safety fieldbus) plus OSSD signals. Guaranteed detection for targets moving 0.1-1.6 m/s (stationary install) or up to 3 m/s (mobile, ≤4 m); optional static-object detection is not guaranteed. Inxpect's regulatory page associates FCC ID 2ANOS-SBV01 with S201A/S201A-W and 2ANOS-S201A with the W/WL types. 60 GHz safety radar for machinery hazard zones (SIL 2 / PL d), used with an Inxpect control unit (ISC-B01/02/03; up to six sensors) that provides OSSD/PROFIsafe/Modbus outputs; reports distance and angle of the closest moving target per detection field and ignores static objects. Detection 0–5 m; angular coverage configurable 10–100°; response <100 ms. Long-range MLR variants are not permitted in the USA/Canada. Later -W/-WL types use FCC ID 2ANOS-S201A.

interface: CAN (EN 50325-5) to control unit; control unit: OSSD, safety fieldbus, MODBUS TCP
notes: 60 GHz SIL 2 / PL d safety radar sensor (Inxpect SRE 200 Series) with a wide vertical field (30-90° programmable, S202A only) and 20-100° horizontal; works only with an Inxpect C2xx control unit (max 5 sensors when an S202A is present). Reports per detection field the nearest target's distance and azimuth plus OSSD signals; static objects ignored by default. Guaranteed detection for targets moving 0.1-1.6 m/s.

interface: CAN (EN 50325-5) to control unit; control unit provides OSSD / fieldbus / MODBUS TCP
notes: 60 GHz safety radar sensor (SIL 2 / PL d, ESPE Type 3) of the Inxpect SRE 200 system: up to six sensors connect over CAN to a mandatory control unit (IP20, indoor) that provides OSSD/fieldbus outputs and a MODBUS TCP register map with the nearest target's distance and azimuth per detection field. Range 0-5 m, programmable 10-100° horizontal coverage, 62 fps; motion-based detection with an optional static-object mode (not guaranteed). Third-party ROS 1 package only (no declared licence).

interface: CAN (EN 50325-5) to control unit; control unit: OSSD, safety fieldbus, MODBUS TCP
notes: 60 GHz SIL 2 / PL d safety radar sensor (Inxpect SRE 200 Series), 10-100° horizontal x 12° vertical, 0-5 m; works only with an Inxpect C2xx control unit (up to six sensors). Reports per detection field the nearest target's distance and azimuth plus OSSD signals; static objects ignored by default (optional static detection not guaranteed). Guaranteed detection for targets moving 0.1-1.6 m/s (stationary install) or up to 3 m/s (mobile, ≤4 m). A public third-party ROS 1 package polls the MODBUS registers.

model: MT5C01-03 60 GHz mmWave radar AoM module
notes: 60 GHz antenna-on-module (15.5 x 7.0 x 2.2 mm) based on TI IWRL6432AOP (2Tx/3Rx), running TI's motion-and-presence out-of-box firmware: point cloud with x/y/z and radial velocity over UART, static clutter removed. Requires 1.2 V, 1.8 V and 1.8/3.3 V IO rails. Typical human-motion range 15 m at boresight, 7 m at FoV edges. Granted 2026-07-24; evaluation board MT5C01E02R1 sold separately.

Cooperative (secondary) 61 GHz radar: two powered units measure the line-of-sight distance to each other (crane/vehicle anti-collision and positioning), not passive obstacles. Single Tx/Rx under a lens, ±7° beam; output is one range (plus confidence and closing velocity) via UDP or Modbus TCP. Same PCB as KY-LOC 1D.02.01 and the primary-radar KY-RAY firmware variants. Not certified for safety-critical use.

61 GHz cooperative (secondary) radar: two powered KY-LOC units measure the line-of-sight distance to each other (e.g. crane / rail anti-collision); it does not detect passive objects. Single lens-focused beam (±7°), one range value with velocity, SNR and confidence over UDP; repeat accuracy typ. ±15 mm, absolute ±50 mm. FCC grant (2021) covers fixed operations; the current lens hardware revision is filed under 2AXR5-1D-01-01.

Cooperative (secondary) 61 GHz radar: a master/slave pair measures the time-of-flight distance between the two units (0.5–150 m); no passive-target detection, angle or velocity output. Wider ±45° x ±15° antenna than KY-LOC 1D.01.01. 138 x 138 x 43 mm, 1020 g; 3 W typical / 5 W max; 64-byte UDP frame and Modbus TCP, full ICD on request. Not certified for safety-critical use.

60 GHz UAV/altimeter-class 4D radar board (50 mm); the maker's U100 family is also sold at 79–81 GHz. The maker states the U-series alternates ±60° and ±30° beams and fuses near/far detections. Output claimed as X/Y/Z/V; no public protocol.

60-64 GHz 4D radar module for UAV altitude sensing and obstacle avoidance (TI IWR6843 on a bare 35x35 mm board); outputs X/Y/Z and velocity for up to 24 tracked targets. Maker store listed US$178 (1-9), US$158 (10-99), US$135 (100-199) on 2026-09-17 but all bands were out of stock. Peak power 3 W; 5-90% RH non-condensing.

interface: PoE (standard PoE per product name; data interface not specified)
notes: 77-81 GHz UAV radar variant with standard PoE, sold by Ningbo Linpowave on Alibaba; specs are marketplace listing attributes (no manual published). Listing output field reads 'X, Y, Z, V'; power attribute '12V 1A'. Title says 250-300 m range. Price $439 (1-9), $399 (10+).

In-cabin human-presence and vital-sign radar (child presence detection, occupant monitoring), sold as a bare 35x35 mm board ('V10 with no case'). Maker's Alibaba listing gives different figures (0.1-20 m, 0.04 m resolution, 0.02 m accuracy, ±60° az / ±25° el); maker product page values used here. Alibaba listing price  for 1-9 boxes (2026-09-23).

77 GHz front-facing 4D radar module (X, Y, Z and velocity output), sold as open board or cased. Maker page is internally inconsistent: spec table lists azimuth FoV 80°, elevation 24°, range 0.2-100 m, resolution 0.4 m, accuracy 0.1 m, while its feature text says azimuth ±60°, elevation ±12°, ±0.18 m accuracy and 0.36 m resolution; the Alibaba listing says 77-81 GHz, 0.4-100 m, elevation ±10°, 0.2 m accuracy. Supply 5 V/1-2 A, 12 V/0.5 A, or 13-30 V option. Alibaba price $219 (1-9), $199 (10+).

77 GHz long-range vehicle/traffic radar (ADAS collision avoidance, roadside traffic monitoring) from Ningbo Linpowave (Lingbo Microstep). Specs here come from the maker's V200-labelled marketplace listing; a Linpowave manual titled V300 but describing V200 gives different values (±70° az, ±50° el, 0.5-200 m, ±55 m/s, TTL/RS422/CAN-FD, -40 to +85 °C).

interface: PoE (standard PoE per product name; data interface not specified)
notes: 77-81 GHz vehicle/traffic radar variant with standard PoE, sold by Ningbo Linpowave; specs are marketplace listing attributes (no manual published). Output field reads 'X, Y, Z, V'; power attribute '12V 1A'. The maker's V300 page lists 'V300 with POE (no case)' as one of four variants. Price $439 (1-9), $399 (10+).

Housed 77 GHz automotive corner radar from Linpowave (Beijing/Ningbo), sold on Alibaba under the LBWB brand; maximum 24 tracked targets. Weight given as ≤200 g; peak current 300 mA at 12 V. Maker product page and Alibaba listing differ on minimum range (1 m vs 0.1 m), accuracy and supply; maker page values used where they conflict.

Housed 76-81 GHz automotive corner radar from Linpowave, sold on Alibaba under the LBWB brand; outputs up to 24 tracked targets, with target height available within 40 m. Linpowave's English site also sells a different 60-64 GHz configuration under the same name 'VJ80' (0.2-100 m, USD 219/229), which should not be merged with this unit.

77 GHz 2T4R blind-spot (BSD/LCA) corner radar; outputs tracked targets and alarms over a proprietary CAN bus, with lamp/buzzer outputs and turn-signal/reverse inputs on a 10-pin Molex Mini50 connector. Pairs as master/slave via an address pin. Pedestrian detection range stated as 100 m. The innosent.com site describing this model is the seller's own English site, not the German company InnoSenT.

Aftermarket two-sensor 77 GHz reverse parking-assist kit (MediaTek MT2706W) mounted with tape behind a plastic bumper; output is an audible buzzer with three distance zones up to 3.2 ft, active below 10 km/h; no data output. Discontinued at Metra but still in distribution. FCC grant requires professional installation.

60 GHz 4T4R people-counting / multi-person tracking module: tracks up to 3 people (counts up to 10) with position, height and speed reports over UART (115200 baud); filters out inanimate objects. Moving-target detection to 5 m (±50° az, ±40° el, ±0.08 m), static-person detection to 3 m (±40° az, ±30° el, ±0.3 m); coverage figure states 100° x 80°. Supply 5 V typ (500 mA typ, 600 mA max). Datasheet notes ranging is 'temporarily' not supported, so effective range may fluctuate.

interface: IO level outputs (alarm lamp, buzzer) + 2 IO inputs (turn signal, reverse gear)
notes: Reseller kit of two housed 77 GHz blind-spot radars (unit label CAR-B53) plus lamps, buzzer and harnesses; price is per kit. Output is alarm levels on IO lines only, no detection list. FoV figures are antenna −6 dB beamwidths. Specs are the OEM (Microbrain CAR-B53-1) product-page values; the listing states DC 12 V supply. Aftermarket dual-radar blind-spot kit (two housed 77 GHz radars plus lamps/buzzer); output is alarm levels on IO lines only, no detection list. FoV figures are antenna −6 dB beamwidths. OEM user manual lists 8–36 V, <5 W, 77–78 GHz, 132.4 g, conflicting with the OEM product page values used here.

77 GHz barrier-gate anti-smash radar (TI IWR1642, 2Tx/4Rx) for parking/garage entrances; outputs two relay contacts plus a single-target RS-485 message; learns the static background and must be re-taught when the scene changes. Detection range 6 m (default 3 m, configurable). The FCC ID covers an ITS-AXX model family (marketing variants) and also carries a forward-collision-warning manual (9–24 V). Superseded by ITS-AX1-2/AX2-2/AX3; maker quotes 3–5 year service life.

Battery-powered (19 Ah Li-SOCl2) LoRaWAN radar distance / liquid-level sensor for tanks, sewers and rivers; single 8° beam reporting one distance value per collection interval (1-1440 min), no angle or velocity output. Radar chip is Acconeer A121 per FCC internal photos. FCC grant restricts use to indoor field-disturbance-sensor operation and prohibits vehicle use. Cellular variant also exists (-35 to +70 °C). Price observed 2026-09-18 at MCCI store (variants marked sold out at the time).

60 GHz (AiP, 4T4R Skyrelay RC6011 chip) indoor people-tracking module: tracks up to 10 people and outputs a point cloud with x/y/z over UART; also detects micro-moving (stationary) people. Detection 0.5-8 m at 2.7 m ceiling height; quick-start guide gives 5 m moving / 3 m stationary radius. Datasheet lists 60-64 GHz; FCC grant covers 57-64 GHz. Average current 110 mA at 100 ms period; supply needs ≥1 A. Key parameters match the Hi-Link HLK-LD6001B module.

60 GHz pedestrian presence sensor for Rectangular Rapid Flashing Beacon crosswalks: single narrow beam aimed at a 4.5-5 ft diameter kerbside zone, output is a dry relay with adjustable hold time (0.2-25 s), 0.2 s initial detection. Radio is the certified InnoSenT IDR-2050 module (FCC UXS-IDR-2050) inside the MS Sedco host. Current draw 75 mA; no IP rating published.

77 GHz compact obstacle-avoidance radar for low-speed vehicles (sweepers, shuttles, mine cars); 3TX/4RX, outputs up to 64 tracked targets per 40 ms frame with target-height filtering; three configurable alarm zones. Also offered as a 32 x 32 x 13 mm PCBA. Brochure body text gives 40 x 40 x 22.5 mm for the finished product vs 24.5 mm in its spec table.

60 GHz multi-lane traffic speed radar module (1-4 lanes) developed by Hunan Nanoradar; the US FCC grant is held by Xiamen Milesight IoT under 2AYHY-MR62-60G and its user-manual exhibit is the Nanoradar MR62 manual. Bare 48 x 52 mm board, 3T4R, outputs up to 32 tracked moving targets (distance, speed, angle, energy) over a 3.3 V TTL UART with a custom protocol (protocol manual separate). Range 30 m at ±30°, 90 m at boresight; moving targets only. Price is for the Nanoradar-branded MR62 at Sensorlidar; whether that unit is the FCC-granted Milesight build is not established.

77 GHz dual-beam (short ±45° to 40 m, long ±9° to 120 m / ±4° to 170 m) obstacle radar; both beams run simultaneously. Outputs up to 64 objects over CAN; angular accuracy ±0.1° long mode, ±0.3°…±1° short mode. Antenna −6 dB beams 18° azimuth (medium range) and 14° elevation. Community ROS1 driver (MIT) available; official protocol manual not public.

77 GHz 3TX/4RX 4D obstacle-avoidance radar for low-speed vehicles; operating mode (cluster point cloud or object trajectory) is set at the factory. Angle measurement range is 120° (azimuth beam -6 dB 120°); the 150° figure applies to pedestrians within 10 m. Two-target radial separation stated as >0.2 m; point-cloud velocity field clips at ±16 m/s. Distributor price US$405 (Cluster with CAN box) / US$342 (Object with CAN box) on 2026-09-17.

interface: Gigabit Ethernet (TCP; UDP point cloud / CAT-240)
notes: Mechanically rotating 77 GHz FMCW scanning radar (33 dBi horn-lens, 3.6° azimuth beam on the certified CIR-F-J antenna) producing 360° 2-D polar power scans and range/bearing/power point clouds; no elevation, no Doppler. 400 or 800 azimuths per rotation; 4.4 cm or 17.5 cm range bins. 24 V DC, 24 W (50 W with heater); 262 x 385 mm, 7.8 kg. Legacy product, superseded by RAS3/RAS6. Grant requires fixed-location mounting and no co-location. Colossus protocol and MIT-licensed IA SDK are public.

Mechanically rotating 76-77 GHz imaging radar (360°, 400 azimuths per rotation, 0.9° sampling, 2.8° azimuth beamwidth) for bulk-materials and mobile automation. Two instrumented ranges: 70 m (0.04 m bins) and 275 m (0.16 m bins); frame rate equals rotation rate, 4 or 10 Hz. Outputs raw FFT, CFAR point cloud (range, bearing, power - no elevation, no Doppler), navigation targets or ASTERIX CAT-240. Single D38999 connector for 24 V and gigabit Ethernet; mounts on 4 x M8 at 101.6 mm PCD. Quote-only pricing.

79 GHz 180°-class short-range automotive radar (reference design) intended to replace up to four ultrasonic parking sensors; also for lateral collision, power-door protection and kick-to-open. On-module processing outputs objects over CAN FD; optional Ethernet and ingress protection are customization options. Sibling ASPER230 is 77-81 GHz, 10 cm-60 m, 20 Hz, CAN FD + Ethernet.

180°-FoV short/mid-range automotive radar platform (reference design) intended to replace up to six ultrasonic sensors and provide corner-radar functions; elevation FoV 60° or 100° depending on configuration; maximum power 3 W. Ingress protection and Ethernet are customization options. Sibling ASPER130 is 76–79 GHz, 25 m, 10 Hz, CAN-FD only. No public ICD/SDK.

77-81 GHz 4D/5D imaging radar with five selectable range modes (short to hyper-long); 5 cm range resolution applies to the short-range mode and 550 m to a mid-sized vehicle at long range. Output is an open UDP/DDS point cloud (x, y, z, radial velocities, SNR); PTP sync, VESA 100x100 mount. Provizio withdrew the hardware product pages in 2025; quote-only, no published price.

interface: Proprietary 3-wire Pulsar transducer bus to a Pulsar controller
notes: 60 GHz FMCW non-contact level transducer for liquids and solids (dBR8: 8 m, dBR16: 16 m); outputs a single distance/level to a Pulsar controller, no angle or velocity. Effective beam 3° with signal processing. Repeatability ±1 mm. 1-inch BSP/NPT thread; ATEX/IECEx/FM variants. FCC grant is for fixed operations only; outdoor use must point vertically down.

interface: UART (1.25 Mbaud); SPI, I2C, CAN-FD on SMT pads
notes: 60 GHz (57-64 GHz configurable; antennas optimized 57-61.5 GHz) SMT module based on TI IWRL6432, 2TX/3RX, preprogrammed with TI's motion and presence detection demo (3D point cloud with x/y/z/doppler, tracker, human/non-human classifier). Requires 1.8 V core supply (up to 1.36 A, configuration dependent) and 1.8 or 3.3 V IO. Datasheet table lists the -12 dB beam widths as 50° (E-plane) and 110° (H-plane). Compatible with TI MMWAVE-L-SDK and TI's mmwave_ti_ros ROS 2 driver.

Aftermarket 79 GHz parking/corner radar kit (two sensors on one harness, single MediaTek MT2706 antenna-in-package SoC, 1Tx/1Rx): no angle measurement; output is a buzzer tone band for the single nearest object (alert ≤1 m on RAR-7000, ≤0.6 m on the front/corner RAR-7001). Mounted behind the bumper with adhesive pads; FCC grant requires professional installation and forbids simultaneous transmission with other transmitters. Product page no longer online; superseded by RAR-7200/8200.

interface: CAN/UART (listed); buzzer/LED outputs and discrete vehicle inputs
notes: 3-in-1 aftermarket 79 GHz blind-spot / lane-change / parking-assist kit (TI AWR1642, 2Tx/4Rx, two angled antenna facets for 180° azimuth): radar head plus ECU box, buzzer and two LED indicators; no detection-level output published although CAN/UART is listed. Modes: BSD/LCA 0.5-20 m with 0.75 m range resolution; PAS 0.2-2 m with 0.05 m. Power <4 W for radar plus ECU; 12 V and 24 V vehicles; AEC-Q100 claimed. Sold at retail in Taiwan for NT$9,980 per kit (2026-09-21).

interface: CAN / UART; LED and buzzer warning outputs
notes: 77 GHz Moving Off Information System (UN R159) kit: faceted radar sensor covering 180° azimuth / 24° elevation with ECU box and LED/buzzer indicator; warns for objects in a 5 m x 5 m zone at vehicle speeds 0–10 km/h; inputs for reverse, turn signals and odometer. 12 V and 24 V systems. Vendor news describes CAN object data (speed, time-to-collision, coordinates), but no ICD is public. The same FCC manual also covers the 79 GHz RPAS model RAR-7203 under a separate grant.

77 GHz Blind Spot Information System kit for trucks/buses (UN R151), mounted at the front-right corner: detection 10 m forward and 30 m rearward, active at 0-30 km/h, tracks up to 10 objects internally but outputs only LED/buzzer warnings. Two TI radar chips (AWR1642 + AWR1843) feed three patch-array panels for 180° azimuth. Radar sensor weighs about 267 g; IP69K applies to the radar sensor unit; 12 V and 24 V vehicles. Quote-only.

79 GHz short-range blind-spot / moving-off radar for heavy vehicles and mobile machinery (UN R159 MOIS); detects, tracks and reports up to 64 objects over J1939 CAN, with five detection zones and two ignore zones configurable. Price is for the PrecoRADAR wired front retrofit kit 6982002A sold on Amazon by the Sensata store (2026-09-19). Another Sentry79 document lists ±14.3 m/s max Doppler velocity; this record uses the current datasheet.

79 GHz side-turn-assist / lane-change radar for trucks (UN R151) with configurable front, centre and rear zones (up to 48 m fore/aft, 4.5 m to the side); reports up to 64 raw targets and tracks per 60 ms cycle over J1939 CAN and drives in-cab alerts; designed to ignore stationary objects and requires vehicle speed and turn-signal inputs. STA mode ±28.6 m/s, LCA mode ±53.6 m/s. Housing about 171.8 x 114 x 70 mm, PC-ABS radome.

interface: 2x CAN 2.0B, SAE J1939 (250/500 kbit/s; 1 Mbit/s option)
notes: 79 GHz side-turn-assist / lane-change-assist blind-spot radar for heavy vehicles (front and rear antenna arrays, 800 MHz chirp): Side Turn Assist below 30 km/h prioritises moving vulnerable road users and ignores stationary objects; Lane Change Assist above. Outputs J1939 target messages per 60 ms cycle over two CAN 2.0B channels; built-in IMU and trailer mitigation. Side detection range 4.5 m; front/rear configurable up to 48 m. TE GET64 12-pin connector. A separate FCC grant (OXZSTA79, 2024) covers the same marketed product name.

76–77 GHz 2T4R blind-spot corner radar (GB/T 39265 BSD) with CAN FD output; targets output in order of distance (default) or RCS. The vendor's 5° angular-resolution claim is high for an 8-virtual-channel array. Antenna −3 dB beam about 80° azimuth. Storage −40…+90 °C; quiescent current ≤0.1 mA. No public DBC/ICD.

61 GHz area-monitoring radar (RMS1000 family; RMS-E is the FCC regional variant, RMS-A ETSI, RMS-C Japan), 3Tx x 4Rx, 120° x 8° aperture. Outputs raw targets with range, azimuth and radial speed (no elevation) over Ethernet CoLa, plus field-based switching outputs; 50 m on 1 m² RCS, 100 m on 10 m². SICK defines resolution such that two targets separate when they differ by more than twice the stated value (0.8 m in range). Public ROS/ROS2 driver (sick_scan_xd).

Wide-angle 77-81 GHz radar for excavators and wheel loaders, built from three radar modules that transmit in turn to cover 170° azimuth; 0.9-13 m detection range. CAN 2.0 object output with X, Y and power per object (no velocity or height field); CAN protocol section marked TBD in the FCC manual. Commercialised 2023 for special-purpose vehicles; grant forbids co-location with other transmitters.

77-81 GHz radar for construction / industrial vehicles built on a TI AWR1443 module (RM14-03A). CAN object table reports up to 20 detected objects with X, Y and power (no velocity or Z field in the documented message), 100 ms configurable cycle. Coverage 120° at 7 m, 30° at 45 m; detection range 45 m vehicle / 22 m pedestrian. Professional installation required; grant forbids simultaneous transmission with other transmitters. SRS web page lists IP69K vs IP68 in the manual.

77-81 GHz collision-warning radar for refuse and heavy vehicles: two RM14-03A (TI AWR1443) modules at right angles in one housing give 180° coverage (10 m for vehicles, 6 m for pedestrians). Outputs a CAN object table with X, Y and power per detected object (no Z, no velocity field). Sold in North America as the 3rd Eye 3EC-IRISt01; quote-only. FCC grant requires professional installation.

77 GHz 4D imaging radar using four radar chips (192-channel MIMO). Long-range mode: car 250 m, 1.40 m range resolution, azimuth 100° (±15° at 250 m); short-range mode: car 100 m / pedestrian 50 m, 0.46 m resolution. Point cloud (X, Y, Z, Doppler, power; up to 3,000 per frame) over 1000BASE-T1 Ethernet with a published frame format; vehicle data in via CAN FD. Output format may be changed on customer request. Professional installation required; grant prohibits co-located transmission.

60 GHz single-chip (TI IWR6843, 3Tx/4Rx) radar module for detecting minute movements / vital signs of people at close range, used in the SE68-51 long-stay occupancy sensor (Seoul subway restrooms). FoV is range-dependent (120° at 3 m, 20° at 5 m); 3 m x 3 m floor area when ceiling-mounted at 2.7 m. Output format not published. FCC single modular approval limited to fixed installations.

60–62 GHz micro-motion (breathing/heartbeat, presence) radar module, 42 x 42 x 8 mm, 14 g, bare PCB to be mounted in a polycarbonate enclosure; detects people to 5 m (3 m x 3 m floor area at 2.7 m height). Storage −40…+85 °C; peak power 3 W. Physically the same PCB as RM68-51 (silkscreened with the older FCC ID); grant depends on firmware. No public output protocol.

61 GHz road-lane vehicle-detection radar module for ITS (traffic monitoring), sold to ITS OEMs since 2022: up to 300 m for passenger cars, lane discrimination within 80 m, narrow 20° beam at 20 m, no elevation output, 2.43 m range resolution. Bare PCB with 10-pin FFC (two UARTs, 5 V). Single modular approval limited to fixed installations; co-located simultaneous transmitters need FCC multi-transmitter evaluation. Output format not publicly documented.

interface: CAN FD + 100BASE-T1 Ethernet (1000BASE-T1 for radar cube)
notes: 77 GHz 4D automotive radar (UMRR-9D platform, antenna Type 152) with long-range mode (0.9-178 m, ≤1.8 m range separation) and medium-range mode (0.33-65 m, ≤0.66 m), ±50° azimuth / ±10° elevation in both. Outputs up to 255 points per ≤55 ms cycle with measured elevation; stationary reflectors reported. FCC single modular grant valid only for OEM integrators; public Apache-2.0 ROS 2 driver.

part_number: UMRRA1A6-A (Housing 18 / Antenna A6 Type 166 / DSP A1)
notes: 77 GHz 4D imaging radar (192-channel virtual array) with three modes: long range 1.8-300 m (separation ≤2.5 m, -400…+200 km/h), medium range 0.5-132 m (≤0.55 m), short range 0.32-88 m (≤0.42 m, ±180 km/h); azimuth ±50° in all modes; direct elevation measurement; up to 1024 points per cycle. Output over 100BASE-T1 Ethernet (smartmicro UDP transport protocol); CAN FD pins present but not yet enabled. Cycle target ≤55 ms, currently ~100 ms. Apache-2.0 ROS 2 driver from smartmicro. FCC single modular grant: OEM installation only. Distributed in the US by AutonomouStuff.

77-81 GHz 4D automotive radar (3TX/4RX) with four modes: long (1.3-130 m, ±65°), medium (0.6-56 m), short (0.2-19 m) and ultra-short (0.1-9.5 m, ±70° az / ±14° el, ±60 km/h). Range separation 1.3 m / 0.6 m / 0.3 m / 0.15 m by mode; update cycle ≤70 ms in long-range mode; processing latency 2-4 cycles. Datasheet allows 24 V (up to 32 V) heavy-vehicle supply; weight <186 g; IP67 only (no IP69K).

part_number: UMRRA4AB-A (Housing 17 / Antenna AB Type 171 / DSP A4)
notes: 77 GHz automotive/industrial radar with three modes: extra-long range 1.2-240 m (separation ≤2.4 m), medium 0.5-98 m (≤1.0 m), short 0.2-42 m (≤0.4 m, cycle <40 ms); azimuth ±50°; direct elevation measurement; up to 255 points per cycle; -400…+200 km/h. Ethernet (100/1000BASE-T1, smartmicro UDP protocol) and CAN FD; Apache-2.0 ROS 2 driver from smartmicro. Shock/vibration listed as 'tba'. Distributed in the US by AutonomouStuff.

4D/PxHD traffic-management radar (UMRR-A4 platform, antenna Type 171) for multi-lane, multi-object tracking on poles/gantries; four range modes from 300 m (≤3 m separation, 2 m minimum) down to 98 m (<1 m separation, 1.0 m minimum) for passenger cars. Sends a detected-target list every cycle via the proprietary smartmicro transport protocol; up to four sensors per COM HUB with separate frequency channels or time slots. US FCC grant covers 76-77 GHz.

77 GHz 4D/UHD front/rear automotive radar with two modes: narrow beam (±16°, 1-175 m, ≤1.8 m range separation, 4° optional azimuth separation, -400...+200 km/h) and wide beam (±50°, 0.5-64 m, <0.66 m separation, 15° optional azimuth separation, -340...+170 km/h). Outputs a target list (point cloud with elevation) and optionally tracked objects every ~55 ms; power 3.75-5 W; Hirose LF10 12-pin IP67 connector. Quote-only via distributors.

77–81 GHz 4D corner/short-range automotive radar with three modes: long 0.8–120 m (<1.2 m separation), medium 0.4–55 m (<0.6 m), short 0.15–19.3 m (<0.3 m); speed range −340…+140 km/h (long/medium) and −400…+140 km/h (short). Azimuth separation ~30° is an option. Optional collision-avoidance firmware provides a 3D occupancy grid (0.15–10 m, 0.5 m cells). Shock/vibration 100 grms / 14 grms; up to three frequency channels for multi-sensor networks. Datasheet in hand is titled UMRR-11 Type 153.

Radar head of STONKAM's PSA27 7-inch HD millimeter-wave radar system kit for commercial vehicles and machinery. Reports the closest object over CAN (1 Mbps default; 250/500 kbps optional); single angle measured, 14° vertical is the antenna fan. Not sold alone; kit offers on the maker's Alibaba store have MOQ 2. FCC grant authorizes 76.0-77.0 GHz.

60 GHz 1-D local positioning radar (crane/vehicle positioning) with a dielectric-lens pencil beam; outputs one distance and velocity per frame, as a primary radar to passive targets or with a secondary-radar partner unit. Bandwidth modes 0.5 GHz (2–50 m) and 2 GHz (1–20 m) under FCC. Not a functional-safety device. Family discontinued (PDN 25_002); successor LPR-1DHP-291.

1-D local positioning radar (LPR) for crane, rail-bound transport and heavy-machinery positioning; lens-focused ±2.5° beam, reports one distance and velocity per measurement, no angle output. Three modes: primary (passive reflector, typically up to 50 m; FCC 2 GHz mode 1-20 m), secondary (two units, up to 300 m) and diversity (four units, up to 500 m). Primary-mode values recorded. Output is a single distance/velocity value rather than a point cloud or track list. Price is the Radwell new-product listing, a reseller rather than the maker.

TI 60 GHz single-chip radar module (IWRL6432 + antenna, 30-pad reflow-mount QFM) for motion and presence detection; host reads the point cloud (x, y, z, velocity, SNR) over SPI via TI's mmWaveULink. Adult-presence range 15 m at boresight, 8 m at ±60°; update rate 1–5 Hz; peak supply current 1 A. Preview status: only the XI prototype part was orderable (out of stock at capture). FCC grant restricts operation to 57.0–59.4 GHz although the device covers 57–61.5 GHz; no co-location allowed; 20 cm separation. Same product as the TI IWRL6432WMOD 60 GHz radar module (2Tx/3Rx, six-element azimuth virtual array, two elevation rows giving coarse elevation). Firmware modes Autonomous / Multi-Zone / Verbose chosen at load time; only Multi-Zone and Verbose emit a point cloud; motion/presence chain removes zero-Doppler (static) returns. Presence range 15 m at boresight, 7–9 m at ±60°; documented update rates 1–5 Hz. Only the XI pre-production part was orderable at capture.

Airport foreign-object-debris (FOD) radar head (12Tx/12Rx, 78–81 GHz) mounted on a tower or vehicle roof; sweeps a fan beam across a 100° field and geo-tags stationary debris on an airfield map to ~2 m, 50–350 m range. Sold as a quoted system with camera, tower, power box and consoles; proprietary software, no public ICD. 3-minute boot; on-site corner-cube calibration.

interface: IO-Link 1.1 (COM3) + 2 switching outputs; SAE J1939 CAN
notes: 60 GHz 3Tx x 4Rx radar scanner for object and position detection; internally forms 3D points but outputs one object (nearest or strongest) with distance, azimuth, elevation, velocity and signal strength over IO-Link and SAE J1939 (PGN 0xFF20), plus six collision radii and three signal fields as switching outputs. Default update 150 ms (2 Hz to 10 Hz configurable). Distance accuracy ±2 mm. Not a safety device. German distributor listed EUR 849.00 at qty 1 on 2026-09-21.

61 GHz FMCW vertically pointing present-weather (precipitation) radar, not an object-detection sensor: it measures individual hydrometeors in a ~2 m column and reports precipitation intensity, accumulation and type. Integrated lens antenna (33 dBi); mount vertically within ±1°; average power 0.5–1.3 W; shock 10 g / 11 ms. Public Modbus register map in the user guide.

60 GHz imaging radar development module built on Vayyar's VYYR720x RFIC: point cloud (X, Y, Z), people tracking, vertical profile and presence over USB 2.0; the vBLU module variant uses SPI. Scanned band is one of 61.0-61.5 GHz or 62.0-63.1 GHz depending on profile; range resolution 13.6 cm at 1.1 GHz bandwidth and ~5.9° angular resolution as given in the vendor spec. Module licensed for development only; FCC single modular approval. Requires a heatsink at ≥40 °C.

Legacy W-band 4D imaging radar with electronic beam steering and six preset range modes (25-600 m); range resolution 0.1-2.5 m and velocity resolution 0.5-2.5 m/s are user-selectable, max unambiguous velocity 5-100 m/s (sign convention not stated). Replaced by the ViSight-3/ViSight-5 line; the PCRS evaluation kit pairs it with a Radar Detection Processor rated 0-30 °C. Weight <700 g, power <20 W.

Pole-mounted stop-bar presence detector covering a small intersection (four approaches, three lanes each, up to 12 controller channels) at 12-15 ft mounting height; outputs zone presence via an Arc2 cabinet interface (SDLC or contact closure), configured with the Windows-only Expanse software. No per-target range, angle, speed or elevation output. Power 50 W with the anti-snow heater. Specification sheet is a Wavetronix document hosted by dealer Orange Traffic.

6TX/8RX (48 virtual channels) 4D imaging radar sold by the maker on Alibaba in Standard/Pro versions, with optional converter (Standard US$300; Standard + converter US$360). Speed accuracy stated 0.05 m/s. Operating band, interface, frame rate and temperature are not published; the listing also claims 360 m detection distance.

interface: CAN FD (5 Mbps data, 1 Mbps arbitration)
notes: Compact short-range 4D imaging radar (M8 6-pin connector). Mode dependent: multimode max range 20–50 m with range resolution 0.04–0.1 m and max Doppler 15–30 m/s; 52 m/s in Doppler-optimised modes; 0.044 m resolution in point-density modes. Up to four units per CAN FD bus (node IDs 0–3), fixed 120 Ω termination (ZPRX-UW-NT variant unterminated); 4.8 W peak; storage −40…+95 °C. Manual lists ±65°/±75° azimuth and ±60°/±75° elevation coverage figures; no public CAN ICD.

interface: CAN FD (1 Mbps arbitration / 5 Mbps data)
notes: Credit-card-size 77-81 GHz 4D radar (CAN-FD / 12 V edition, long-range antenna only); up to four units per CAN-FD bus. Range resolution/accuracy apply to high-density modes and Doppler figures (158 m/s ambiguity, 0.2 m/s resolution) to Doppler-optimised modes. Angular resolution 2° x 4° is defined for targets in adjacent range-Doppler cells. Not the same product as the marketing 'zSIGNAL 2.0'. Datasheet lists FCC Part 15 as pending.

77 GHz 3T4R housed radar module with TTL UART (4-wire 100 mm lead), up to 32 targets; speed accuracy 1 km/h; operating current ≤120 mA @ 12 V. Spec table gives module dimensions 30 x 30 mm; mechanical drawing gives 35.5 x 35.5 x 17 mm housing with 4 x M2.5 holes. Protocol available on request only. Distinct from the larger ZLYMRR400.
